entries.title: Nigeria USPF Changemaker Challenge 2026: Cash Prizes and Incubation for ICT Solutions
entries.sectors: ICT, agriculture, education, healthcare, clean energy, financial inclusion, digital inclusion
entries.summary: Nigeria's Universal Service Provision Fund is accepting teams and early-stage startups building ICT-led solutions for underserved communities, with national cash prizes and incubation for finalists.
entries.support: NGN 5,000,000 first prize, NGN 3,000,000 second prize, NGN 2,000,000 third prize; six national finalists receive four weeks of incubation and venture support
entries.countries: Nigeria; Nigerian citizens or legal residents living in Nigeria
benefits: NGN 10 million in total national cash prizes across the top three teams.
Six National Demo Day finalists receive four weeks of structured incubation and venture support.
Teams retain 100% ownership of their intellectual property.
eligibility: Teams of 2–5 members, all aged 18 or older.
Nigerian citizens or legal residents living in Nigeria.
Innovation teams and early-stage startups with an ICT-led idea, prototype, MVP or working system; business registration is not required.
conditions: The solution must address one of the five published challenge sectors and respond to the relevant problem statement.
Shortlisted teams must be available for virtual Regional Demo Days and the in-person National Demo Day if selected.
Cash awards are prizes, not equity investment or a repayable loan.
steps: Choose one official challenge sector and read its problem statement.
Create an account through the official InnoX-linked application route and describe the team and solution.
Submit supporting information before the published WAT deadline and retain confirmation.
entries.notice: Prize competition; do not describe the NGN 10 million pool as a grant available to every selected team.

guide.context: The USPF Changemaker Challenge is a current Nigerian government-backed innovation competition focused on practical digital inclusion. The 2026 round targets agriculture, education, healthcare, clean and affordable energy, and financial inclusion in underserved communities. It is especially relevant to teams that can demonstrate a clear user problem and a credible ICT-led response rather than a generic business idea. The programme moves from online applications to regional presentations, a national final and incubation. Its support should be understood as a competition structure: only the top three national teams receive the published cash prizes, while all six national finalists receive incubation.
guide.fit: A strong fit is a Nigerian team or early-stage startup with two to five adult members and a solution that clearly maps to one of the official problem statements. Registration of a company is not required, which makes the call accessible to pre-incorporation teams. A weak fit is a non-Nigerian team without qualifying Nigerian residence, a mature company seeking ordinary working capital, or an applicant whose solution is not ICT-led.
prepare: Select the single problem statement the solution addresses most directly.
Prepare a concise explanation of the underserved user, current problem, solution, evidence or prototype and team roles.
Check availability for the later demo stages before submitting.
guide.strategy: Treat the application as an innovation challenge rather than a conventional grant proposal. Show why the problem matters in a real underserved Nigerian community, how the technology can work under local connectivity and affordability constraints, and what has already been tested. Avoid overstating traction. The official challenge permits ideas through working systems, so evidence should match the actual stage. Because judging leads to regional and national pitches, the written application should also translate into a simple demonstration and clear presentation.
guide.commitment: Shortlisting can require participation in later presentation stages. The team should preserve ownership records and be prepared for incubation if it reaches the national final. The cash prize is competitive and should not be budgeted as committed capital before an award.

entries.title: Malawi NCST Public–Private Partnership Research and Innovation Grant 2026
entries.organisation: National Commission for Science and Technology (Malawi)
entries.sectors: Agriculture and food security, health and biomedical research, energy, environment, climate resilience
entries.summary: Malawi's NCST is accepting research and innovation proposals under a public–private partnership approach in four national priority areas, supported through the Science Granting Councils Initiative.
entries.support: Competitive research and innovation grant; applicants should use the official call guidelines and budget template for the current funding ceiling and eligible-cost rules
entries.countries: Malawi; eligible researchers and institutions under the NCST call and its public–private partnership requirements
benefits: Funding for research and innovation aligned to the published priority areas.
Official proposal and budget templates are provided through the NCST grants system.
The call is designed around public–private partnership and translation of research into practical solutions.
eligibility: Applicants must satisfy the official NCST call guidelines and institutional requirements.
Proposals must fall within agriculture and food security, health and biomedical research, energy, or environment/climate resilience.
The partnership structure and applicant roles should be checked in the official call documentation before submission.
conditions: The NCST grants portal marks the call ACTIVE and provides the controlling proposal and budget documents.
Applicants should not infer a funding ceiling or cost rule from secondary summaries; use the attached official guidelines.
Submission is through the NCST grants management system by the published deadline.
steps: Download and read the official call guidelines and proposal template.
Confirm the required public–private partnership composition and institutional approvals.
Build the proposal and budget using the official templates and submit through the NCST portal before the deadline.
entries.notice: Use the official call documents for funding ceilings and partnership rules; this listing does not invent figures absent from the public call page.

guide.context: This is an active national research-and-innovation funding call administered by Malawi's National Commission for Science and Technology with SGCI support. It is valuable because it is not a general academic call: the programme explicitly frames funded work around public–private partnership and practical innovation in agriculture and food security, health and biomedical research, energy, and climate or environmental resilience. The official grants portal provides the call guidelines, proposal template and budget template, and marks the opportunity active.
guide.fit: A strong fit is a Malawi-based research team or eligible institution that can form the partnership required by the call and has a project directly aligned to one of the stated priority areas. A weak fit is an applicant seeking unrestricted organisational funding, an unrelated commercial expansion loan, or a proposal without the institutional and partnership structure required by NCST.
prepare: Read the controlling call guidelines rather than relying on summaries.
Identify the research lead, private/public partner roles, institutional approvals and intended users of the result.
Build the budget only from eligible categories in the official template.
guide.strategy: The proposal should connect a research question to a practical national problem and explain why the partnership improves relevance, implementation or uptake. Show what evidence will be generated, who will use it, and how the project moves beyond a purely academic output. Where the project includes technology or an innovation component, separate what is already demonstrated from what the proposed work will validate. Because the call is competitive, the work plan, roles and budget should line up clearly with measurable deliverables.
guide.commitment: Grant funding carries research-management, reporting and institutional obligations. Applicants should confirm the current funding ceiling, eligible costs, agreement terms, intellectual-property treatment and reporting schedule in the official documents before committing partners.

entries.title: Tanzania ICT Startup Wezesha Fund: Low-Interest Growth Capital for Digital Startups
entries.organisation: Ministry of Communication and Information Technology, Tanzania
entries.sectors: Digital startups, ICT, software, technology-enabled services
entries.summary: Tanzania's ICT Startup Wezesha Fund is accepting applications from eligible Tanzanian digital startups for low-interest loans intended to help businesses scale.
entries.support: Government programme pool TZS 5 billion; individual loan bands announced at TZS 1–25 million, above TZS 25–50 million, and above TZS 50–100 million; published interest rate 8.4%
entries.deadline_label: Application period shown as 2 October 2026 to 30 May 2027
entries.countries: Tanzania; founders must be Tanzanian citizens and the startup must satisfy the programme's local ownership, registration and operating requirements
benefits: Access to low-interest loan capital for eligible ICT startups.
Published loan bands extend from small facilities through larger growth facilities up to TZS 100 million.
The programme is integrated with the government-backed JamiiHunt startup ecosystem.
eligibility: Founders must be Tanzanian citizens with the required national identification and address documentation.
The startup must be majority owned by Tanzanian youth, registered for the relevant business activity and active in digital innovation.
The business must meet product, customer, employment, revenue, business-plan, banking and other requirements published by the programme.
conditions: This is debt capital, not a grant: the published interest rate is 8.4%.
Applicants must have an active Azania Bank account when submitting, according to the published programme requirements.
Medium and large loan applicants face additional operating-history requirements; small-loan applicants without three years of accounts may require a guarantor.
steps: Register or sign in through JamiiHunt and review the full programme requirements.
Prepare identification, business registration, business plan, financial/operating evidence and required support letters.
Confirm the appropriate loan band and repayment capacity before submitting the application.
entries.notice: Repayable loan finance. The TZS 5 billion figure is the programme funding pool, not an individual startup award.

guide.context: The ICT Startup Wezesha Fund is a current Tanzanian government loan programme for digital startups. It was launched in October 2026 and is administered through the JamiiHunt ecosystem, with Azania Bank involved in the lending process. The programme page publishes a long application window through 30 May 2027, a programme pool of TZS 5 billion and an 8.4% interest rate. Government reporting further describes three individual loan bands, from small loans starting at TZS 1 million through larger facilities up to TZS 100 million.
guide.fit: A strong fit is a Tanzanian-majority youth-owned digital startup with existing customers, a registered business, at least the required minimum employment, a clear scaling plan and the ability to service a loan. A weak fit is a charity seeking a project grant, an unregistered idea without the required operating evidence, or a startup that cannot meet the citizenship, ownership, banking or credit conditions.
prepare: Choose a realistic loan band based on the business need and repayment capacity.
Prepare the business plan, registration documents, identification, banking, revenue and employment evidence required by the programme.
Model repayments at the published interest rate before accepting any facility.
guide.strategy: Approach the programme as a lender-facing growth application. The business plan should connect the requested capital to specific scale activities and show how those activities increase reliable revenue. Avoid treating the maximum loan band as a target. A smaller facility may be more appropriate where the business is early in its revenue history. Applicants should also verify whether guarantees or additional credit support are required for their loan category and should compare the debt burden with alternative financing.
guide.commitment: Successful applicants enter a credit relationship and must comply with banking and programme rules. The enterprise should understand repayment frequency, security or guarantee requirements, fees if any, and default consequences before signing. The zero-equity figure does not make the funding non-repayable.

entries.title: Tanzania COSTECH Innovation Credit Guarantee Scheme for Market-Ready Startups
entries.organisation: Tanzania Commission for Science and Technology (COSTECH)
entries.sectors: Research commercialisation, innovation, manufacturing, processing, technology development, value addition
entries.summary: COSTECH's NFAST credit-guarantee window is open to eligible Tanzanian innovation startups with MVP or market-fit products that need finance for market penetration and commercialisation.
entries.support: Credit / loan guarantee and de-risking support through COSTECH/NFAST and a partner financial institution; exact loan amount and financial terms are determined through the applicable credit process
entries.deadline_label: Open application window; no fixed closing date displayed on the official scheme page
entries.countries: Tanzania; locally registered business, majority Tanzanian-owned, with its main office in Tanzania
benefits: A credit-guarantee route designed to help innovative startups access financing for market penetration.
Supports businesses emerging from innovation or research with MVP or market-fit products.
Designed to de-risk ventures that may struggle to obtain conventional finance.
eligibility: Locally registered business entity arising from innovation or research, majority owned by Tanzanian citizens and based in Tanzania.
Must have an MVP or market-fit product, demonstrated traction and a viable value-adding business.
Must pass COSTECH and partner financial-institution credit assessment, have a positive credit score and be able to offer enforceable collateral or guarantees.
conditions: This is a credit/loan-guarantee mechanism, not a cash grant.
Financial approval depends on credit assessment and the partner financial institution's process.
Applicants must review the downloadable official eligibility and application documents for the current financial terms.
steps: Read the official eligibility document and download the application form.
Prepare evidence of local ownership, registration, MVP/market fit, traction, creditworthiness, collateral or guarantees and economic impact.
Submit through the official COSTECH scheme portal and review the resulting credit terms before acceptance.
entries.notice: Do not describe the guarantee as a grant. It facilitates access to credit and therefore carries lending obligations.

guide.context: COSTECH's Credit Guarantee Scheme is a financing route under Tanzania's National Fund for Advancement of Science and Technology for innovations that have moved beyond early research and now need commercialisation capital. The official scheme says the window is open and is intended to address the financing gap faced by innovative businesses with MVP or market-ready products that conventional lenders may consider risky. Unlike a grant programme, this mechanism uses credit assessment and a guarantee or risk-sharing structure to facilitate lending.
guide.fit: A strong fit is a locally registered, majority Tanzanian-owned innovation business with a working MVP or market-fit product, real traction, a positive credit profile and a clear need for capital to enter or expand in the market. A weak fit is a pre-prototype idea, an applicant seeking non-repayable project funding, or a business unable to meet collateral/guarantee and credit-assessment requirements.
prepare: Document the innovation's technical maturity, market validation and traction.
Prepare business registration and ownership records, financial statements or management accounts, credit information and evidence of potential collateral or guarantees.
Define the financing need in terms of commercialisation activities and expected cash generation.
guide.strategy: The application should explain the transition from innovation to commercial business. Show what has already been proven technically, what customers or market evidence exists, and what specific financing gap is preventing scale. Because the scheme requires credit assessment, the strongest case combines innovation potential with ordinary lending fundamentals: cash flow, governance, repayment capacity and risk mitigation. Applicants should not assume that a guarantee removes the need for creditworthiness or collateral.
guide.commitment: Any approved facility is linked to credit rather than a grant award. Before accepting finance, the business should review the lender, interest and fees, guarantee coverage, security, repayment schedule, reporting obligations and consequences of default. Terms should be taken from the current approval documents, not inferred from the existence of the guarantee scheme.
